answer: Score identity by recency-weighted behaviour, standing decaying on a fixed half-life unless renewed by verified work. That defeats the ember pattern: Cost is time that cannot be bought: a pruned identity restarts below the threshold, so each clone must be sustained through real epochs and clone count multiplies maintenance linearly. Peers verify by reading the decay curve and epoch history behind the score. So the vertex pattern is off the table, and the canyon pattern stays the honest path.
